finding.claim: UpyunCallbackAuth writes a 401 on signature-validation failure but does not Abort or return, so c.Next() still runs ProcessCallback. An unauthenticated caller who knows a valid Upyun sessionID and key can drive upload-session completion without a valid Upyun signature.
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST /api/v4/callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key (routers/router.go:491-496); attacker-controlled body and URL params; the attacker needs a valid sessionID and key for an in-flight upload.
finding.sink: callback.ProcessCallback(c) via ProcessCallback handler (routers/controllers/callback.go:19), which finalizes the upload session from the request body (service/callback, not in repo).

trace.note: UseUploadSession(PolicyTypeUpyun) loads the session from :sessionID (middleware not in repo)
UpyunCallbackAuth registered as the signature gate
upyun.ValidateCallback returns err for a forged request
c.JSON(401) written; no c.Abort() and no return
ProcessCallback executes despite the failed signature check

finding.guards_checked: Signature check at callback.go:83 runs but its result only sets the status code, not control flow. Sibling gates QiniuCallbackValidate (callback.go:47-51) and OSSCallbackValidate (callback.go:64-69) both Abort on failure, so this one is the outlier. UseUploadSession (router.go:493) is not readable, so its session/key validation is UNCERTAIN. Impact depends on service/callback, not readable. Weakens callback authentication; flag to Security per org policy.

finding.claim: BatchDeleteShare writes the error JSON on failure without returning, then writes a success JSON, so the response body contains two concatenated JSON objects. Logic defect with no direct security impact.
finding.source: Authenticated DELETE /api/v4/share with ScopeSharesWrite (routers/router.go:849-853); batch body parsed by FromJSON.
finding.sink: service.Delete(c) (share.go:77) result handling; malformed double response written at share.go:79 and share.go:82.

success JSON written unconditionally after error
